claim: Ma Chik = Machig Labdrön, great yogini, founder of Chöd
evidence: Machig Labdrön (Ma gcig Lab sgron, 1055-1149) was a yogini who originated the Chöd lineage.

claim: nine serial absorptions = mthar gyis gnas pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa dgu = navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti
evidence: 84000 glossary gives nine serial absorptions as navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti, mthar gyis gnas pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa dgu.

claim: (note is translation of the passage itself; no external fact)
Ananda is the Buddha's disciple foremost in wisdom
evidence: Ananda is foremost in conduct, attention to others, memory, erudition and resoluteness; Sariputra is the one foremost in wisdom.
correction: Ananda is foremost in learning/memory (hearing), not wisdom; Sariputra is foremost in wisdom.

claim: Sanskrit title Ārya-kuśalamūla-saṃparigraha-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra with the given Tibetan title
evidence: 84000 Toh 101 'Upholding the Roots of Virtue' is Kuśalamūlasaṃparigraha; exact Tibetan title wording not directly seen.

claim: right efforts = yang dag par spong ba = samyakprahāṇa
evidence: yang dag par spong ba is the Tibetan for samyakprahāṇa/samyakpradhāna (right efforts).

claim: text likely refers to Bonpo medicinal methods
evidence: No source found tying this passage to Bon medicine specifically.

claim: Anagami (non-returner) will not be reborn in the desire realm
evidence: The non-returner is reborn in a pure abode and does not return to lower realms, having eliminated sensuous desire and ill-will.

claim: The Fourth Jewel refers to the Guru, equal to the Three Jewels
evidence: Guru as fourth jewel is a common idea, but I did not fetch a source.

claim: perfection of concentration = bsam gtan gyi pha rol tu phyin pa = dhyāna-pāramitā
evidence: Dhyāna is practiced as fifth perfection (dhyānapāramitā); Tibetan bsam gtan.

claim: Sanskrit mantra transliterated into Tibetan
evidence: 'Kamam Gayonaya Gaya' could not be identified as a Sanskrit mantra.

claim: Sharadvatiputra is also known as Sariputra, a main disciple
evidence: Śāriputra is sometimes called Śāradvatīputra; one of the two chief disciples.

claim: Kadampa is a major school of Tibetan Buddhism founded by Atisha
evidence: Atisha is the most important founding figure, but Dromtön, his disciple, led and institutionalized the school (Radreng, 1056).
correction: Founded by Dromtön on the basis of Atisha's teachings; Atisha is its inspirational founding figure.

claim: (gloss 'will suffer greatly' is paraphrase; no external fact)
Enjoyment body = Sambhogakaya; Emanation bodies = Nirmanakaya
evidence: Standard equivalence of longs sku/sambhogakaya and sprul sku/nirmanakaya; context names Enjoyment Body and Emanation Bodies.

claim: syllables are Sanskrit dharani kept in transliteration
five deeds of immediate retribution = five most heinous sins, e.g. killing mother or father
evidence: Killing mother, father, an arhat, drawing a buddha's blood, causing schism; also called actions of immediate retribution.

claim: perfection of ethics = tshul khrims kyi pha rol tu phyin pa = śīla-pāramitā
evidence: śīlapāramitā (T. tshul khrims kyi pha rol tu phyin pa).

claim: Tushita is the Joyous Heaven where Bodhisattvas dwell before final birth
evidence: Tuṣita is where all Bodhisattvas destined for enlightenment dwell before their final life.

claim: emptiness of non-discarding = dor ba med pa stong pa nyid = anavakāra-śūnyatā
evidence: anavakāraśūnyatā, Tibetan dor ba med pa'i stong pa nyid, one of the sixteen/eighteen emptinesses (non-dispersal/non-rejection).

claim: Garab Dorje, the first human teacher of Dzogchen
evidence: He is described as the first human to receive the complete Dzogchen transmission and the first teacher of Dzogchen (traditionally).
